name: Lakeside Drive Boardwalk
start: Buckland Drive or the town foreshore
summary: The Mallacoota Shared Pathway skims Bottom Lake with raised boardwalks, fishing platforms and views to Howe Range, Rabbit Island and Goat Island. It links town and Karbeethong, then meets The Narrows.

name: Tim Peach Walk to Bastion Point
start: Devlin Drive or Bastion Point car park
summary: A town-to-coast loop through littoral rainforest to Bastion Point, Mallacoota's main swimming beach, rock pools and clifftop picnic tables looking over the inlet entrance, Gabo Island and the Howe Range.

name: Bastion Point to Lake Barracoota
start: Bastion Point, or Big Beach by water taxi
summary: The long northern beach walk: across the inlet mouth to Big Beach, then 15 km of open sand and dune country to Victoria's largest freshwater coastal lake.

name: Mallacoota Coastal Walk
start: Betka Road end, or the Betka River picnic area
summary: The 9.3 km line of beaches south of town — Tip, Davis Creek, Betka, Quarry, Secret and Pebbly — walked in one go or, as most people do it, a beach at a time.

name: The Narrows Walk
start: Buckland's Jetty, Lakeside Drive
summary: A local favourite along the waterway that joins Mallacoota's Bottom and Top Lakes, with shoreline views, birdlife and a restored boatshed picnic stop. Continue to Captain Creek Jetty for the longer version.

name: Shipwreck Creek Heathland Walk
start: Shipwreck Creek Day Visitor Area
summary: A half-hour loop out of the Shipwreck Creek campground through heathland that carries an extraordinary spring wildflower show, including rare and threatened orchids.

name: Old Coast Road Walk
start: Shipwreck Creek Day Visitor Area
summary: The old road line from Shipwreck Creek back towards Mallacoota, running through heathland into bloodwood forest with Wilderness Coast views and some of the best birdwatching in the park.

name: Shipwreck Creek to Seal Creek Walk
start: Shipwreck Creek Campground
summary: The half-day walk out of Shipwreck Creek through banksia woodland and heath to a secluded beach with some of the best rock pools on this coast.

name: Genoa Peak Walk
start: Genoa Peak car park
summary: A steep forest climb with rock hopping, ladders and broad views over Mallacoota Lakes, Gabo Island and the coast.

name: Gabo Island Lightstation Walk
duration: About an hour each way, or a full day with the island
start: Gabo Island boat harbour, at the northern end
summary: An island walk under the second tallest lighthouse in Australia, built from the pink granite it stands on, above one of the largest Little Penguin colonies in the world.

name: Wingan River Rapids Walk
start: Car park on Boundary Track
summary: Down through fern gullies to the Wingan River, where the track narrows and is marked in places by rock cairns, ending at cascading rapids you can explore up or downstream.

name: Nadgee Wilderness Walk
start: Merrica River trackhead, off Newtons Road
summary: The New South Wales half of this coastline's great walk — four days of untouched shore between the Merrica River and Mallacoota, through declared wilderness with a permit and a hard cap on numbers.

name: Lake Elusive Walk
start: Small car park on West Wingan Road, 3 km from the Wingan Inlet campground
summary: Through tall eucalypt forest to a white sandy beach on Lake Elusive — at up to 21 metres, the deepest dune-blocked coastal lake in Victoria.

name: Rame Head Walk
start: Western end of Fly Cove, Wingan Inlet
summary: Through coastal forest from Fly Cove out to the trig point on Rame Head, the big blunt headland that anchors this stretch of the Wilderness Coast.

name: Mount Everard Walk
start: Car park on Mount Everard Track, off Cicada Trail
summary: A climb through forest and heathland to a large sloping rock face with views over Point Hicks and the Thurra dune fields.

name: Bittangabee Bay to Green Cape Walk
start: Bittangabee Bay, Green Cape area
summary: The southern leg of the Light to Light, linking a sheltered rocky bay to the lightstation, passing remnants of the old horse-drawn tram track along the way.

name: Thurra River Dunes Walk
start: Thurra River Campground, near campsite 14
summary: Coastal banksia and heathland opening into a dune field that towers 30 metres above the Thurra River — a landscape with nothing else like it on this coast.

name: Point Hicks Lightstation Walk
start: Lightstation Reserve gate, Point Hicks Road
summary: Out to the tallest lighthouse on the Australian mainland, past the monument, on the headland James Cook's party recorded as the first part of eastern Australia they sighted in 1770.

name: Saros Track
start: Grassy area 100 m west of the Point Hicks Lightstation
summary: A short track to a view over the wreck of the SS Saros, which ran ashore here in heavy fog in 1937 on its way to Sydney.

name: Light to Light Walk
start: Boyds Tower picnic area, Green Cape area
summary: The far south coast's signature walk — three days of red rock cliffs, eucalypt forest and coastal heath between two lighthouses, from Boyds Tower to Green Cape.

name: Boyds Tower Walk
start: Boyds Tower picnic area, Edrom
summary: A short, graded stroll to the sandstone tower Benjamin Boyd built above the sea in the 1840s, at the northern end of the Light to Light Walk.

name: Clinton Rocks Walk
start: Tamboon Inlet, reached by boat — or a 150 m walk in from Clinton Rocks Track
summary: Giant granite boulders covered in brilliant orange lichen, on a beach most people never reach, with the Point Hicks light tower visible down the coast on a clear day.

name: Pinnacles Loop Walk
start: Pinnacles Road carpark, Pambula-Haycock area
summary: A short loop above The Pinnacles, where white sand sits on orange clay in a gully cut open by erosion — the most striking piece of geology on this stretch of coast.
